parts.text:
You read part of an interview. An analyst asked one future user of a software service a series of questions. You decide, for each question, whether it follows up the answer given just before it.

A question follows up the previous answer when it asks about something that answer said: it asks the speaker to explain, give an example of, say more about, or say why of something the answer mentioned, or it picks up a particular thing the answer named. Wording does not matter; a question can follow up an answer without repeating any of its words.

A question does not follow up the previous answer when it turns to something that answer did not mention, even if the speaker said it in an earlier answer, even if it stays with the same broad subject, and even if it is a good question. A general question that could follow any answer, such as whether there is anything else, does not follow up either.

You receive the pairs of the interview after its first question: for each later question, the answer given just before it, and the question.

Reply with JSON only: an object with one key, "questions", a list with exactly one entry for every pair, in the same order. Each entry has "id", the question's id, and "follow_up", true or false.

Q2
The answer just before it: I keep our drones and charging equipment in working order. My work involves adding new drones to our fleet, retiring old ones, setting up charging pads at our sites, and sending drones to charge. I also take drones out of service for repairs and put them back afterwards.
The question: When you arrive at work at the start of your shift, what is the very first thing you do?

Q3
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: Who tells you what needs to be worked on when you start your day?

Q4
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: Could you tell me about the worst day you have had at work in the last few months?

Q5
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: What is something you currently check by hand because you do not trust automated information?

Q6
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: When you think about a new software system being introduced, what concerns or worries do you have about what it might do wrong?

Q7
The answer just before it: I worry about radio coverage being patchy around ports, industrial sites, and in bad weather, and about reports from drones arriving late, out of order, more than once, or not at all. I also worry that the links used to give instructions to drones and charging equipment are unreliable, meaning an instruction might get through twice and the sender often cannot tell if the first attempt arrived. Additionally, the service runs on a single server, gets updated and restarted during working hours while drones are flying, and occasionally crashes.
The question: Right after something goes wrong with a drone or charging pad, what specific information do you need to know?

Q8
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: Once you finish repairing a drone, who do you notify or hand it over to?
